text: CPD method regression-based approach estimating price parities. underlying statistical model \[ p_{ij} = PPP_j \times p_i \times \epsilon_{ij} \tag{1}\] \(PPP_j\) purchasing power parity arbitrary region \(j\), (\(r = 1,...,j,...,R\)), \(p_i\) average regional price arbitrary commodity \(\), (\(n = 1, ..., , ... N\)), \(\epsilon_{ij}\) independently identically distributed random variable.1 Taking logs Equation 1 yields \[ \begin{aligned} ln p_{ij} & = ln PPP_j + ln p_i  + ln \epsilon_{ij} \\ & = \alpha_j + \gamma_i + ln \varepsilon_{ij} \end{aligned} \tag{2}\] \(\alpha_j\) price level region \(j\) relative regions comparison. \(\alpha_j\) can also expressed relative reference region, example, national price level. , \(\alpha_j\) represents subnational purchasing power parity region \(j\) given \(\hat{PPP}_j = exp(\hat{\alpha}_j)\). CPD model Equation 2 may interpreted fixed-effects specification, country effects yield estimates subnational purchasing power parities, commodity-specific effects generate estimates subnational price levels. model can written regression equation explanatory variables take form dummy indicators region commodity. \[ \begin{aligned} ln p_{ij}  = & \alpha_1 D_1 + ... + \alpha_j D_j + ... +\alpha_R D_R + \\ & \eta_1 \mathcal{D}_1 + ... + \eta_i \mathcal{D}_i + ... + \eta_N \mathcal{D}_N + \varepsilon_{ij} \end{aligned} \tag{3}\] \(\varepsilon_{ij}\) independently identically (normally) distributed zero mean variance \(\sigma^2\), , \(\varepsilon_{ij} \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\). variables interest, \(PPP_j\), can estimated parameters \(\hat{\alpha}_j\) using ordinary least squares (OLS); see Section 1.1.3 Implementation. pricelevels package (Weinand 2025) can used estimate subnational purchasing power parities, can also computed using standard OLS outlined examples 1 2. Estimating sPPPs with `pricelevels`, with weights -------- dt1[, cpd(p = price, r = region, n = product, w = weight)] #>         1         2         3         4         5  #> 1.0187925 0.8460806 1.1784210 0.9964223 0.9880038  #
